documents.title: Generative AI Policy (Policy 312)
documents.stance_why: The page lists five principles (privacy, transparency, integrity, fairness, human oversight) and says "the use of AI tools is encouraged" with conditions such as disclosure and no protected data. It sets no per-course rule and does not hand the decision to instructors, so it permits AI use with conditions.
documents.summary: A short university IT-governance policy listing five principles for GenAI use by faculty, staff and students: protect data, disclose use, uphold integrity, verify output and keep human oversight. It says AI use is encouraged but sets no course-level rules.

units.why: The opening sentence says the university "supports the responsible use of Generative Artificial Intelligence" for teaching, learning, research and administration. It is an institution-wide framework statement of purpose, so P56 rather than P02, since it sets a principle and not a default rule for coursework.
units.anchor: supports the responsible use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
units.frag_start: Binghamton University supports the responsible use

units.why: "The input of personal, sensitive, or confidential information ... is prohibited unless approval has been granted" bans entering protected data into GenAI. It binds everyone, applies while working and is must-not. It is a data-protection rule (P50), not an upload-of-course-materials rule (P49).
units.anchor: input of personal, sensitive, or confidential information (Protected Information)
units.frag_start: The input of personal, sensitive

units.why: "approval ... must be granted by Information Security" and "a proper risk review must be completed and documented" set a vetting procedure before GenAI processes Protected Information. It is a data-protection and vetting rule, so P50, with must.
units.anchor: a proper risk review must be completed and documented
units.frag_start: To safeguard data security and privacy

units.why: "While the use of AI tools is encouraged" states a welcoming default toward AI use, so P02 with informs and unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: While the use of AI tools is encouraged
units.frag_start: While the use of AI

units.why: "Clearly disclose when GenAI tools are used in academic work, research, or other university activities" is a duty to disclose AI use with each submission (P24), must, binding all.

units.why: "Use GenAI in ways that align with Binghamton's academic integrity policies as well as New York State IT policies" ties AI use to existing rules. It is a framework principle (P56); P36 does not fit because it does not classify any AI use as misconduct.
units.anchor: align with Binghamton's academic integrity policies as well as New York State IT policies

units.why: "ensuring work reflects your own effort and understanding" requires that submitted work be the person's own. P29 (ownership) is chosen over P30 because it does not ask for line-by-line explanation.

units.why: "Verify GenAI outputs for accuracy and fairness" tells users to check AI output, which is P31. It is phrased as an imperative, so must.
units.anchor: Verify GenAI outputs for accuracy and fairness
units.frag_start: Verify GenAI outputs for accuracy

units.why: "actively reducing bias to support equitable outcomes" names bias as a concern users must act on. P53 is chosen over P31 because the point is reducing bias, not checking factual accuracy.
units.anchor: actively reducing bias to support equitable outcomes
units.frag_start: Verify GenAI outputs for accuracy

units.why: "qualified humans must review and approve any decisions or actions based on them" keeps people as final decision-makers over AI output. P32 (AI must not replace human decision-making) fits; P46 covers only grades and this is general.
units.anchor: qualified humans must review and approve any decisions or actions
units.frag_start: Treat GenAI outputs as advisory

documents.title: Gen AI and Your Syllabus (sample syllabus statements)
documents.stance_why: The page offers sample syllabus statements in three groups and says instructors decide: "some instructors may want to allow ... and others may want to prohibit". It sets no stance itself, so it delegates, with three tiers.
tiers: Can use in certain instances or specific ways
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance giving instructors sample syllabus wording for allowing, partly allowing or banning generative AI, with reminders about verification, privacy, cost and rationale. The choice is left to each instructor.
